costGuide.title: Land Rover 508PN Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 508PN typically takes 14-18 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for a 508PN engine replacement is the condition of the timing chain assembly and the cooling system components located in the V8 valley. Units where the early-style hydraulic tensioners have been upgraded to the revised post-2013 specification, and the plastic coolant crossover pipes replaced with aluminium, command a slight premium but carry significantly lower long-term risk. Because this is a complex, all-aluminium V8, a full 508PN rebuild requires specialist machining and precision timing work. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for a detailed breakdown of what influences your final quote.

failures.title: Land Rover 508PN Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear (2009-2012 models)
items.whatHappens: The early hydraulic timing chain tensioners on the 5.0L V8 are prone to losing oil pressure, particularly on cold starts or if oil change intervals have been extended. This allows the timing chains to stretch and slap against the plastic guides, producing a distinct rattling noise from the front of the engine. If ignored, the guides can shatter, leading to chain skip and catastrophic valve-to-piston interference.
items.repairVsReplace: Updating to the revised, mechanically locking tensioners introduced in 2013 is a known preventative measure. If the rattling has been present for some time and chain stretch is confirmed, a full 508PN engine replacement or comprehensive top-end rebuild is the only reliable solution.

items.title: Coolant Crossover Pipe Leaks
items.whatHappens: The plastic coolant crossover pipes located deep in the valley of the V8 become brittle with age and intense heat cycling. They eventually crack, leading to rapid, often invisible coolant loss down the back of the engine block, which can quickly escalate to severe overheating and cylinder head warping.
items.repairVsReplace: Upgrading to machined aluminium crossover pipes is a standard and highly recommended preventative repair. If overheating has already occurred and caused head gasket failure or block distortion, a full unit replacement is required.

items.title: Water Pump and Thermostat Housing Degradation
items.whatHappens: The composite plastic thermostat housing and the water pump impeller are subject to the same intense V8 valley heat as the crossover pipes. The housing can crack or warp, breaking the seal and causing external coolant leaks, while the water pump bearing can fail, leading to noisy operation and reduced coolant circulation.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the water pump and upgrading to an aluminium thermostat housing is a routine maintenance item for the 508PN. It rarely necessitates engine replacement on its own unless the resulting coolant loss was ignored until the engine seized.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2013 revisions of the 5.0L V8 architecture received updated, significantly more durable timing chain tensioners and revised cooling system routing, making later examples vastly more robust than the early 2009-2012 production run .
failures.cta: Compare rebuilt 508PN prices with the failure already addressed

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 508PN
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible on the passenger side near the engine mount, or listed on the VIN plate under the bonnet. The 508PN is frequently confused with its supercharged sibling, the Land Rover 508PS (which features a Roots-type supercharger in the V8 valley and entirely different intake plumbing), or the Jaguar-designated AJ133. While the AJ133 and 508PS share the same 5.0L block architecture, fitting a supercharged engine into a naturally aspirated 508PN chassis requires extensive ECU remapping, different engine mounts, upgraded fuel systems, and altered cooling architecture. Exact code matching is critical to avoid costly installation errors and immediate running faults.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 508PN - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 508PN is only advisable for lower-value hosts or project builds, and must come with verifiable proof that the timing chain tensioners have been upgraded to the post-2013 specification and the coolant crossover pipes replaced. Without this documented history, the risk of inheriting a stretched chain or a cracked plastic coolant pipe is unacceptably high. Explore our vetted used 508PN engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned 508PN directly addresses the core weaknesses of this generation. It will include upgraded mechanical timing chain tensioners, machined aluminium coolant crossover pipes, and a refreshed water pump and thermostat housing. This is the most sensible, cost-effective route for preserving a Range Rover or Range Rover Sport without the unpredictability of a used unit. Compare reconditioned 508PN options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples showing signs of bore wear, or if the engine has already suffered overheating damage from a failed crossover pipe. A quality rebuild should include line-boring, new pistons and rings, and a complete overhaul of the valvetrain and cooling system to exceed factory specifications. Discuss a custom 508PN rebuild

items.question: What is the most common failure on the 508PN?
items.answer: The dominant failure patterns on the 508PN are timing chain tensioner wear on pre-2013 models and coolant crossover pipe degradation. Early hydraulic tensioners can lose pressure, causing chain stretch and a distinct cold-start rattle that can lead to catastrophic valve damage. Plastic coolant crossover pipes in the V8 valley become brittle with age, causing rapid coolant loss and severe overheating. Post-2013 revisions feature significantly more durable timing components and improved cooling routing.

items.answer: The 5.0L naturally aspirated 508PN V8 was fitted to the Range Rover (L322 and L405) and Range Rover Sport (L320 and L494) between 2009 and 2022. It served as the premium petrol baseline, delivering smooth, linear power and refined cruising capabilities. It is mechanically distinct from the supercharged 5.0L variants found in SVR or high-spec models. Always verify your specific chassis code before ordering a replacement unit.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 508PN engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned 508PN is strongly recommended over a used unit to proactively address the known cooling system and timing chain weaknesses. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting degraded plastic coolant pipes or early-style hydraulic tensioners. Proper reconditioning upgrades these specific weak points with machined aluminium crossover pipes and revised mechanical tensioners. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, unlike the 3-6 months typical for used engines.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the 508PN and not the supercharged 508PS or AJ133?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet or the stamped code on the engine block near the engine mount. The 508PN is visually identifiable by its naturally aspirated intake manifold, lacking the large Roots-type supercharger sitting in the V8 valley. It is commonly confused with the 508PS or AJ133, which share the same block but have entirely different forced-induction plumbing and ECU mapping. Fitting the wrong revision will cause severe compatibility and mapping issues.
